data.title: Grown Rogue Announces New York Cannabis Acquisition Agreement
data.description:
Grown Rogue International ( (TSE:GRIN) ) has shared an update.

On November 23, 2026, Grown Rogue New York, LLC, a 51%-owned subsidiary, signed membership-interest and asset purchase agreements with PharmaCann and related parties to acquire 100% of PharmaCann of New York’s membership interests and other business assets, including its New York cannabis licenses, Hamptonburgh cultivation and processing facility, and four dispensaries. Completion remained subject to Office of Cannabis Management approval and other closing conditions.

Closing required OCM approval of GRNY as a true party in interest and transfer of license control, simultaneous completion of both agreements, treatment of unpaid taxes, lien releases and no material adverse effect on PCNY. The purchase price was $1.8 million in cash, reduced from $3.1 million for PharmaCann’s 50% share of an approximately $2.4 million New York adult-use cannabis tax assessment and $0.1 million of equipment lease reimbursements. Under an August 20, 2026 agreement, GRNY agreed to provide operational, general and administrative consulting and a secured working-capital line of credit of up to $9.0 million; by November 23, it had begun supporting the operating transition, including cultivation restart at Hamptonburgh.

data.title: AI Financial Announces CFO Transition and Fiscal Year Change
data.description:
The latest update is out from AI Financial Corporation ( (AIFC) ).

Effective November 23, 2026, Steven Plumb transitioned out of AI Financial Corporation’s chief financial officer role and into the same role at Drew Therapeutics Corporation, the company’s biotechnology subsidiary. Tony Isaac, AI Financial’s chief executive officer and a director, assumed the acting chief financial officer role without a change in compensation.

The company changed its fiscal year from a 52/53-week year to a calendar year, moving the 2026 year-end from December 26 to December 31 and setting subsequent year-ends for December 31. The board approved the change on November 23, 2026, in accordance with the company’s bylaws.

data.title: Opendoor Technologies Announces $300 Million At-the-Market Offering
data.description:
An update from Opendoor Technologies ( (OPEN) ) is now available.

On November 27, 2026, Opendoor Technologies entered a Sales Agreement with Virtu Americas LLC as sales agent and/or principal, allowing the company to offer and sell, at its discretion, up to $300 million of common stock. The agreement permits sales through an at-the-market offering, with Virtu eligible to receive commissions of up to 2.0% of gross sales prices.

The company established the offering to complement existing capital resources and provide flexibility to access equity markets opportunistically when market conditions are attractive and sales are viewed as being in stockholders’ long-term interests. Opendoor is not required to sell shares, and the timing and amount of any sales will depend on market conditions and other factors.

data.title: TOP Ships Announces Pistiolis Family Ownership Rises to 61.3% After Series G Conversion
data.description:
Top Ships ( (TOPS) ) has provided an announcement.

TOP Ships is an international owner and operator of modern, fuel-efficient “ECO” tanker vessels transporting crude oil, clean and dirty petroleum products, and bulk liquid chemicals. On November 25, 2026, it announced that it had issued 1,250,000 restricted common shares after a trust benefiting family members of President, CEO and director Evangelos Pistiolis converted 2,000 Series G Perpetual Convertible Preferred Shares.

Following the issuance, outstanding common shares totaled 2,590,567, while Pistiolis and the family trust beneficially owned 1,587,142 shares, or 61.3%. data.title: QHSLab Reports Nine-Month 2026 Financial Results Amid Losses
data.description:
An update from QHSLab ( (USAQ) ) is now available.

On November 27, 2026, QHSLab reported unaudited financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Total revenue increased 13.4% to $2,253,347, ISP revenue rose 63.9% to $1,287,692, gross margin improved to 67.9%, and interest expense decreased 90.0%; net loss totaled $119,021 versus $99,156.

ISP revenue represented approximately 57% of total revenue, while combined allergy diagnostic kit and immunotherapy revenue decreased 19.3%, and third-quarter total revenue fell 8.1%. Operating expenses increased 32.7%, cash declined by $445,693, and total liabilities decreased 54.7%; the Company said substantial doubt remained regarding its ability to continue as a going concern without sustainable positive operating cash flow or additional financing.

data.title: Jaguar Health Faces Nasdaq Delisting Over Listing Concerns
data.description:
Jaguar Animal Health ( (JAGX) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 20, 2026, Nasdaq staff notified Jaguar Health, Inc. that it had determined to delist the company’s common stock under Listing Rule 5101, citing public-interest concerns. The concerns involved a September 17 reverse stock split to avoid noncompliance with the $1 bid-price requirement, followed shortly by a special dividend of Series R convertible preferred stock that staff viewed as having the effect of a forward split and again leaving the bid price below $1.

Nasdaq staff also cited substantial dilution imposed on shareholders since January 2023. Jaguar Health requested a hearing by the November 27 deadline, which under Nasdaq procedures will stay suspension pending the Panel’s decision; the release said the company could not assure continued listing or compliance with other Nasdaq rules.

data.title: Carnival Amends CEO’s Performance-Based Restricted Stock Award
data.description:
Carnival ( (CCL) ) has shared an announcement.

On November 24, 2026, Carnival Corporation Ltd.’s Compensation Committee approved an amendment to CEO Josh Weinstein’s special performance-based restricted stock unit grant made in August 2022. The amendment aligned the award’s performance conditions with those of the fiscal 2024 executive grant, set the performance period to end on November 30, 2026, rather than November 30, 2027, and set vesting for December 2026.

The amended award uses 2026 Adjusted ROIC, adjusted EBITDA per available lower berth day and greenhouse gas intensity reduction goals established in fiscal 2024. It reduced the maximum payout from 200% to 180%, or 900,000 shares, set vesting for December 21, 2026, subject to continued employment, required share retention until December 21, 2028, and added a clawback if Weinstein voluntarily resigns before February 15, 2028.
